extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners designing or evaluating automated reviewer-assignment systems (conference organizers, journal editors, algorithm designers)
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, modeling, and evaluating automated reviewer-to-proposal assignment methods (similarity computation, representation choices, and optimization algorithms) for peer-review settings such as conferences, journals, and grant review panels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Similarity score as objective weight
rubrics_metrics.description: The weight of the edge between a proposal and its reviewer shows the relevance between them (s_ij); the ORAP typically maximizes the cumulative sum of these similarity scores for matched pairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similarity scores form the input weight matrix for optimization; approaches assume availability of a proposal-reviewer similarity score matrix. Exact optimization (ILP/MIP) or heuristics can be used to maximize total similarity. Implementations: TPMS, EasyChair, HotCRP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer workload constraint
rubrics_metrics.description: Each reviewer should be assigned a pre-determined number of proposals (workload w).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforce as constraint ∑_i x_ij = w for each reviewer j (equation 7-3). Essential practical constraint in most mathematical models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal demand constraint
rubrics_metrics.description: Each proposal should be reviewed by a certain number of reviewers (d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforce as constraint ∑_j x_ij = d for each proposal i (equation 7-2). Frequently attempted to be met in models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-stage framework (weighted bipartite graph then assignment)
rubrics_metrics.description: First construct a weighted bipartite graph between proposals and reviewers (weights = similarity), then determine a final assignment optimizing an objective under constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This canonical formulation underpins many ORAP approaches and clarifies separation between scoring (IRRAP) and optimization (ORAP).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximizing cumulative sum of similarity scores
rubrics_metrics.description: Optimization objective to maximize the total similarity across all assigned proposal-reviewer pairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commonly formulated as ILP/MIP. Solved by exact solvers for small instances or approximation/heuristic algorithms (greedy, genetic, ant colony, particle swarm, hybrid methods, network flow formulations) for large-scale problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximizing topic coverage (coverage ratio)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality measured by set-coverage ratio: the ratio of proposal topics covered by assigned reviewer group to total proposal topics (Coverage(q_i) formula 7-4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derive topic sets from keywords or topic models. Use MaxTC-PRA, WGRAP, CMACRA or constrained network-flow transformations to ensure aspect coverage of proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidence (topic coverage confidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure of how much each assigned reviewer's competence encompasses proposal aspects (Confidence(q_i) formula 7-5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computed as average overlap between proposal topics and each reviewer's topics normalized by group coverage; used as constraint or objective alongside coverage to ensure per-reviewer competence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimizing fairness (max-min / lexi-min / rank-maximal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Objective to ensure no proposal is disadvantaged (e.g., maximize utility of worst-off proposal or maximize minimum total similarity per proposal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formulations include max-min fairness, lexi-min, rank-maximal assignments and fairness objective Γ_S(A) = min_i ∑_{j∈R_A(i)} s_ij (equation 7-7). Algorithms like PeerReview4All use incremental max-flow to achieve provable guarantees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum similarity threshold constraint
rubrics_metrics.description: Impose strict constraints on the minimum similarity of valid proposal-reviewer matches to avoid assignments with near-zero relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to prevent assignments where a proposal has zero similarity to all assigned reviewers; can be enforced as a hard constraint in optimization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balanced workload distribution / fairness in workload
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure balanced distribution of review assignments among reviewers to avoid overloading a few experts in popular fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model via upper and lower capacity limits or workload balancing objectives (e.g., minimize difference between max and min total profit/probabilities per reviewer).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict-of-Interest (COI) handling / minimization
rubrics_metrics.description: Include COI constraints or minimize conflicts when generating assignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: COIs should be explicitly modeled (for example, Pradhan et al. include minimizing COIs in an equilibrium multi-job assignment); treat COI edges as forbidden or highly penalized in the weight matrix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation choice: word-based, topic-based, semantic-based
rubrics_metrics.description: Different document representations (frequency-based VSM, topic models like LSI/PLSA/LDA, and semantic/ontology-based) impact similarity computation and assignment quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frequency-based methods ignore word order and suffer sparsity; LDA widely used to identify topics; semantic methods (ontologies, semantic kernels) can enrich profiles but ontologies are costly to maintain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combining word and semantic information
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine LDA/topic models with semantic models (SLM, TF/IDF, semantic kernels) to obtain more accurate similarity scores between reviewers and proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: LDA+SLM, LDA+TF/IDF, exact matching (SLM) + semantic matching (graph/ontology). Time-aware/topic-based weighting of recent publications can improve reviewer profile accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neural network-based language models / word embeddings
rubrics_metrics.description: Use embeddings and deep models (Word2Vec, FastText, BERT, SciBERT, Doc2Vec, SPECTER, etc.) to produce dense vector document representations for similarity computation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These models address sparsity and capture semantic/syntactic affinities; studies show embeddings often outperform classical semantic-based methods. Also includes sentence-pair models and supervised approaches using field association signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of network-based / social information
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage citation, co-authorship, collaboration, committee membership and other social/academic network relationships to strengthen reviewer recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Techniques include topical PageRank, three-layer networks combining semantic, social and citation networks, co-authorship collaborative filtering and connectivity matrices; useful to capture implicit relationships not in text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of optimization/modeling paradigm (ILP, MIP, network flow, set covering, equilibrium models)
rubrics_metrics.description: Select mathematical model appropriate to the objective: ILP/MIP for sum-similarity maximization, network-flow formulations, set-covering for joint panelist objectives, equilibrium/multi-job assignment for balanced profits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small instances: exact solvers (CPLEX). Large instances: approximations, greedy, hybrid or specialized network-flow transforms. Choice affects solvability and runtime; some formulations are NP-hard for certain objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithm class and scalability tradeoffs
rubrics_metrics.description: Algorithms (exact, greedy, stochastic, hybrid, evolutionary, metaheuristic, row/column generation) trade off solution quality versus runtime and memory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Greedy and heuristics scale but may sacrifice optimality; hybrids can improve precision but often increase time. Examples: greedy, two-phase stochastic-biased greedy, genetic algorithms, ant colony, particle swarm, PeerReview4All, FairFlow, row/column generation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group-based multi-aspect assignment vs independent assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Assigning reviewers to proposals independently can harm global workload balance and topic distribution; multi-aspect group-based formulations (CMACRA, WGRAP, MARTA-LRA) aim to optimize group coverage under global constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group-based models consider the committee as a whole and use coverage/confidence measures; typically harder (NP-hard) and approximated via greedy or specialized algorithms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling multi-domain/multilabel reviewer expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Model reviewers and proposals as belonging to multiple research domains (multilabel) and use hierarchical/transparent representations to capture this structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use hierarchical embeddings (e.g., Hiepar), bidirectional GRU with attention, or multilabel classifiers to capture multi-domain expertise and assign reviewers accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freshness / recency weighting of reviewer profile
rubrics_metrics.description: Weight more recent publications higher to reflect reviewers' current interests or use proxies like journal impact factor to measure reviewer 'freshness'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time-aware models (e.g., time-aware topic models) can improve matching to current interests and help diversify reviewer assignment across topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of field labels / supervised label information
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate known field/discipline labels for reviewers and proposals to improve classification and matching quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods like WMD–CCA use field labels to predict relationships; supervised signals can help learn field associations better than purely unsupervised approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision-science techniques for uncertainty and multi-criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply fuzzy optimization, AHP, OWAs and related multi-criteria decision methods to handle uncertainty in expertise and trade-offs among objectives (similarity, cost, budget).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: fuzzy ILP to maximize similarity while minimizing panel cost subject to budget; AHP to combine expertise and relevance into scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation metrics beyond objective value (statistical accuracy / ability to identify best proposals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess assignments not only by optimization objective but also by statistical guarantees about correctly identifying top proposals and robustness to noise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PeerReview4All provides statistical assurances for identifying best proposals; fairness objectives should be evaluated for downstream selection accuracy, not only summed similarity.
